title: Relative left lifting maps over small direct categories induce left lifting colimit maps
statement: Let $\mathcal B$ be a category admitting all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and let $T$ be any class of its morphisms. Write $\mathcal L={}^{\square}T$ for the maps with the left lifting property against every member of $T$, with the diagonal property as in [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. Let $K$ be any small category equipped with a function $e:\operatorname{Ob}K\to\mathbf N$ strictly increased by every nonidentity arrow; neither its objects nor its morphisms are required to be finite. For $D:K\to\mathcal B$, define $L_kD$ to be the colimit of the domain diagram on the full subcategory of $K/k$ obtained by deleting $1_k$, with commuting triangles as morphisms. For a natural transformation $f:A\to B$, suppose that every relative latching map $A_k\amalg_{L_kA}L_kB\to B_k$ belongs to $\mathcal L$. Then the induced map $\operatorname{colim}_K A\to\operatorname{colim}_K B$ belongs to $\mathcal L$. The assertion includes the empty category. No factorization, weak equivalence, model structure or finiteness hypothesis is required.
